My First Month as an Intern: 设计工作室的第一份实习:入职培训、导师带教与第一次独立完成任务。

Last June I started a two-month internship at a small design studio. On my first morning, I was given a name badge, a desk in the corner of the open-plan office and a laptop that barely worked. The induction session lasted an hour: safety rules, the time sheet system, and where the coffee machine hid.

My supervisor, Marta, became my mentor for the summer. She believed that interns should touch real work from day one, so on Wednesday she handed me a small task: redesign a menu card for a local cafe. It sounded easy until I saw the client's brief, which contained seventeen requests on a single page.

My first draft came back covered in comments. Marta had written "good bones, wrong voice" at the top. She sat with me for an hour and explained that design is a conversation, not a performance. I cut the number of fonts from five to two, and suddenly the card looked calmer and more professional.

By the end of the month, the cafe owner approved version six. Marta presented it to the team meeting and mentioned my name first. I realised then that the internship was not about making coffee or perfect first drafts. It was about learning to listen, revise and try again.
